### [llm-anthropic 0.27](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/24/llm-anthropic/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-24

Version 0.27 of the llm-anthropic Python plugin adds compatibility with the anthropic v1.0.0 SDK release.

- Updates the underlying Anthropic Python library dependency to version 1.0.0 or higher.
- Adapts to Anthropic's SDK shift from using httpx to httpx2, matching a similar v3.0.0 update by OpenAI.
- Automated the code migration and passing tests by prompting Fable 5 in Claude Code using Anthropic's official migration guide.

**Why it matters:** Plugin users can upgrade to the anthropic 1.0.0 SDK and benefit from its updated httpx2 networking stack without breaking their LLM CLI workflows.

### [Quoting Drew Breunig](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/23/drew-breunig/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-23

Drew Breunig highlights a shift in AI development where high model costs, exemplified by Fable, force developers to strategically allocate coding tasks rather than relying on cheaper, next-generation models to fix harness issues.

- Prior to Fable, developers relied on cheaper, improved models to solve coding harness and context strategy issues.
- Fable offered high capability but at a significantly higher cost point.
- Alternative models like Opus, 5.6, K3, and GLM proved sufficient for most standard coding requirements.
- High costs led developers to explicitly evaluate which specific tasks to delegate to premium versus standard models.

**Why it matters:** Developers must now optimize context strategies and task routing across different models rather than assuming raw model upgrades will economically solve harness limitations.

`llms` `fable` `llm-pricing` `ai-development`
